summary: Al-free ternary reference austenitic steel Fe-30Mn-1.2C (wt.%) from the rapid alloy prototyping (RAP) combinatorial study, aged at 450 °C for 24 h in air followed by oil quenching. It serves as the baseline for assessing how Al additions and aging affect low-density Fe-Mn-Al-C TWIP steels; the key question here is how long-time, low-temperature aging affects the tensile response of the ternary reference.
composition: Nominal composition Fe-30Mn-1.2C (wt.%), with no Al addition (0 wt.% Al). Fe is the base element; Mn (30 wt.%) and C (1.2 wt.%) are the principal alloying additions that stabilize the fcc austenite and enable the TWIP effect. As the Al-free member of the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl series, it defines the density baseline (no Al-induced density reduction) against which the Al-containing low-density grades are compared.
processing: Synthesized by vacuum-induction melting (VIM) and casting under 400 mbar Ar, using a stepwise movable Cu-mold arrangement to produce five alloys from a 4-kg ingot in one operation (the remaining melt is adjusted by charging Al through an air lock; for this 0-Al alloy no Al charge applies). The cast 10×50×130 mm³ blocks were hot rolled at 1100 °C into 2±0.1 mm-thick, ~500 mm-long sheets, then reheated to 1100 °C and water quenched. Segments (2×60×55 mm³) were cut perpendicular to the rolling direction, homogenized at 1100 °C for 2 h under Ar followed by water quenching, and finally aged in air at 450 °C for 24 h followed by oil quenching; scales were removed by low-pressure fine-grit sandblasting. This aging condition is one cell in a 45-condition matrix (450/500/550/600 °C × 0/1/24 h); its precursor/benchmark state is the as-homogenized condition (1100 °C/2 h, water quenched).
microstructure: Fully recrystallized single-phase fcc austenite with an average grain size of ~20 µm and some retained Mn microsegregations; no cracks, pores, or macrosegregations were found. The parent as-cast material had a coarse dendritic microstructure, which hot rolling and water quenching converted into the fully recrystallized state. Because the Al content is 0 wt.% (below 5 wt.%), a single austenite phase prevails at room temperature; no ferrite or Al-dependent κ-carbide precipitation is expected in this Al-free reference, distinguishing it from the higher-Al members of the series.
properties: Mechanical testing was performed at room temperature at an initial strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1, with all plotted values representing averages of three measurements per state; hardness and tensile screening were complemented by XRD on the rolling plane (samples ground to 1 mm thickness) for phase characterization and metallographic cross-sections perpendicular to the rolling direction. Compared with the as-homogenized benchmark (360 MPa YS, 830 MPa UTS, 77% TE), aging at 450 °C/24 h leaves the yield strength virtually unchanged and slightly increases hardness (~200 HBW), but reduces UTS and total elongation. No explicit numeric YS/UTS/TE values are printed for this exact 450 °C/24 h condition; the sample is represented through the qualitative aging trends reported in the text (Fig. 3's color key includes 450 °C/1 h but not 450 °C/24 h).
mechanisms: Hot rolling at 1100 °C followed by water quenching transforms the coarse as-cast dendritic structure into a fully recrystallized single-phase austenite with ~20 µm grain size, retaining only some Mn microsegregations.

Because the alloy contains 0 wt.% Al (the <5 wt.% Al regime), a single fcc austenite phase prevails at room temperature and no Al-dependent κ-carbide or ferrite formation occurs, so it remains a SIMPLEX-type (TWIP) austenitic steel.

Aging the Al-free Fe-30Mn-1.2C alloy leaves the yield strength virtually unchanged and slightly increases hardness, but reduces UTS and total elongation; this embrittlement becomes most apparent for long aging times (24 h) and higher temperatures (>500 °C), so the 450 °C/24 h sample represents the long-time, lower-temperature aging condition.
conclusions: This 450 °C/24 h condition shows that aging does not strengthen the Al-free ternary Fe-30Mn-1.2C steel: yield strength remains virtually unchanged and hardness rises only slightly, while UTS and total elongation decrease (embrittlement). The best mechanical behavior for this alloy is the as-homogenized state (360 MPa YS, 830 MPa UTS, 77% TE). Its behavior is opposite to that of Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al, which strengthens strongly during aging via κ-carbide precipitation, underscoring that the aging response of the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl system depends strongly on Al content and heat treatment. As the 0-Al reference, this sample provides the baseline in the RAP screening of low-density austenitic steels.
unmapped: In the Fig. 4 strength–ductility map, the Al-free Fe-30Mn-1.2C series ('T + t' 24 h aging trend) spans roughly 490 MPa at ~8% elongation to ~800 MPa at ~70% elongation as a broad trend line, not a specific 450 °C/24 h datum.
